todo: Obtain qualified-human citation verification for the proposed acanthosis-nigricans to type-2-diabetes association.
Confirm the individual's insulin-resistance phenotype and independently diagnose type 2 diabetes before any publication decision; do not infer causation from a skin finding alone.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-25 adds this relationship only as a bounded insulin-resistance association. Acanthosis nigricans is commonly associated with insulin resistance and may accompany type 2 diabetes, but a skin finding does not establish diabetes, its cause, or an individual medical nexus. Require documented acanthosis nigricans, independently established type 2 diabetes using accepted diagnostic criteria, compatible metabolic phenotype and chronology, and review of obesity, medications, endocrine disease, genetic syndromes, and malignancy-associated acanthosis. Do not infer diabetes from acanthosis nigricans alone or treat this association as proof that the skin condition caused diabetes.
evidenceGaps: Independent dermatologic documentation of acanthosis nigricans and laboratory-confirmed type 2 diabetes
Hemoglobin A1c, fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, insulin-resistance findings, and chronology
Assessment of obesity, medications, endocrine disorders, genetic insulin-receptor disorders, and other causes of acanthosis
Review for atypical, abrupt, extensive, or mucosal disease that could indicate malignancy-associated acanthosis

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented acanthosis nigricans, independently established type 2 diabetes, compatible metabolic phenotype/chronology, and competing-cause review; do not infer diabetes from a skin finding alone.

sourceReferences.citation: Leung AKC, Lam JM, Barankin B, Leong KF, Hon KL. Acanthosis Nigricans: An Updated Review. Curr Pediatr Rev. 2023;19(1):68-82. PMID 36698243. doi:10.2174/1573396318666220429085231.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-25 clinical review for the bounded acanthosis-nigricans to type-2-diabetes proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 36698243; updated review describing acanthosis nigricans and its association with insulin resistance/diabetes; approved ME-25 guard requires independent diabetes diagnosis and competing-cause review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited dermatology review supports acanthosis nigricans as a clinical marker associated with insulin resistance and diabetes, without establishing that acanthosis nigricans caused type 2 diabetes in an individual.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; independent metabolic diagnosis, chronology, phenotype, and alternative-cause review are required.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Acanthosis nigricans may reflect hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance that can coexist with or precede type 2 diabetes, but the direction and individual metabolic contribution remain hypothesized until laboratory and clinical findings are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The cited review treats acanthosis nigricans as a marker of insulin resistance and related systemic disease, not as proof that the skin condition caused an individual's diabetes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent skin and diabetes diagnoses; metabolic laboratory findings; chronology; assessment of obesity, medications, endocrine and genetic disorders; and review for atypical malignancy-associated acanthosis.
